title: Queue (FIFO)
intuition: First-In, First-Out: the earliest element added is always served first.
whyExists: Asynchronous event queues, print spooling, and Breadth-First Search (BFS) require fair chronological processing without starvation.
analogy: A line at a grocery store checkout: the first person to stand in line is the first person served.
coreIdea: A Queue maintains two distinct boundaries: FRONT (where elements are removed via dequeue()) and REAR (where elements enter via enqueue()). Array implementations often use modular arithmetic (idx + 1) % capacity to create a circular buffer.

complexity.reason: Circular pointer wraparound avoids shifting existing elements on dequeue.

pitfalls: Dequeuing from an empty queue without safety guard.
Neglecting circular wraparound causing artificial overflow when front has advanced.
Confusing front and rear pointer roles.
